audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Yasuo all seven rows while content and the packet both gave rows 5 and 6 to Aurelion Sol — and full phases[6].why already read 'You are the scaling endgame' underneath a row labelled Yasuo.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol wins 57.59% over 1337 games. Yasuo genuinely owns levels 1-6: Sweeping Blade dashes 475 off any minion and is back in 0.5s at rank 5, two Steel Tempest stacks knock up, and Last Breath blinks 1400 to any airborne target. From the first item the beam outranges all of it, and from two items the Stardust curve passes his flat crit damage.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side and phases[6].side moved Yasuo -> Aurelion Sol to match win[5]/win[6], with phases[5].why rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named 'Starsurge' and 'Comet of Legend' (pre-rework Aurelion Sol abilities), and spikes[1] claimed Last Breath 'resets his own knockup chain'.
audit.why: Riot's Last Breath text says it grants maximum Flow but RESETS all stacks of Gathering Storm — it clears his knockup stacks, it does not reload them. The real spike is the 1400-range blink, the airborne hold, and the 30s cooldown at rank 3.
audit.corrected: Both fabricated names removed and the Last Breath description replaced with what the ability actually does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers stated opposite facts about Wind Wall. The full layer's tldr says it does NOT block your beam; content said four separate times that it 'negates your ranged poke' and 'blocks your Q poke entirely'.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks projectiles. Not one Aurelion Sol ability carries the projectile flag — Breath of Light is a channelled beam, the black hole is a zone, Falling Star is a zone. So Wind Wall blanks his support's poke and covers Yasuo's approach, but it does nothing to Aurelion Sol's own damage. The full layer was right and content was wrong.
audit.corrected: Every content claim that Wind Wall stops your damage removed or inverted; wants.foe[1] rewritten to what Wind Wall actually buys him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Way of the Wanderer's moving shield was never mentioned, and neither was the Sweeping Blade re-hit restriction.
audit.why: His passive shields on damage taken, which absorbs the front of any burst window; and Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds, so once he has burned the near minions his dash chain has a real gap.
audit.corrected: Shield noted in the audit and the re-hit gap written into dosFull[0].d as the actual green light for the beam.
sources: brief enemyKit P and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit and told the reader to hold poke until Wind Wall is spent — advice built on the false blocking claim.
audit.why: Real numbers: Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17, Sweeping Blade 0.5 down to 0.1, Last Breath 70/50/30, Steel Tempest a flat 4s at no cost.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around those numbers, with the poke advice reversed to match the real interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were other fields' strings under unrelated titles; dontsFull[0].d, ahead, breakdown.carry and breakdown.feeding were name-swap templates.
audit.why: Copy-paste bleed and the template sweep.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten from Yasuo's kit at the same length.

edits.after: Once you finish your first item your range and burst punish his approach before he closes the gap, and Wind Wall does nothing here — none of your abilities is a projectile, so he has no answer to a real trade.

edits.before: Fully stacked with Comet of Legend, your global execute and ranged burst outscale his flat crit-based damage entirely, and his all-in windows become predictable and easy to play around from range.
edits.after: Fully stacked with The Skies Descend, your knockup-and-melt pattern outscales his flat crit damage entirely, and his all-in windows become predictable — a 17s Wind Wall cannot cover every step he needs.

edits.before: Yasuo's mobility and Wind Wall let him close the gap on your ranged kit and completely negate your Starsurge poke, and once he lands a Steel Tempest knockup his all-in damage output punishes your lack of early burst, so you're forced to play very defensively and avoid overextending through the laning phase.
edits.after: Yasuo's mobility lets him close the gap on your ranged kit — Sweeping Blade dashes 475 through any minion and comes back in half a second — and once he lands a Steel Tempest knockup his all-in punishes your lack of early burst, so play defensively and never overextend through laning.

edits.after: Level 6 makes this worse, not better — Last Breath blinks him to any airborne target from 1400 range and holds you up there, and at rank 3 it is only a 30s cooldown, so a single Steel Tempest knockup snowballs into a kill long before your Stardust curve threatens him back; respect his all-in windows closely.

edits.after: Your first item finally gives you the range and burst to punish his gap-closes before he lands a combo, and Wind Wall was never an answer to you — nothing in your kit is a projectile; by two items and full Stardust your knockup-into-Q burst clearly outscales his flat crit damage, turning his all-in from a real threat into a predictable, dodgeable cooldown.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Check it before every step-up. - W Astral Flight is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5, and blocks nothing you cast — spend your poke through it. - Sweeping Blade is off cooldown in 0.5s, so his gap-close is never down. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 but only 30s at rank 3.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by making his dashes land nowhere: Sweeping Blade needs a target, and a stacked black hole plus The Skies Descend deletes what he lands on.

edits.before: If Yasuo opens the score, reset expectations and respect Wind Wall doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with E executes and stay relevant through the stardust curve.
edits.after: If Yasuo opens the score his crit items come early and every Steel Tempest hurts, so stop stepping up at all: clear the back line with E from 750 and let him shove into your tower for free.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Yasuo on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, take the wave: Yasuo needs minions to dash on, so shove with E executes, deny him the melee line, and force him to walk at you with no minion to ride.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-hit the same target for a few seconds — once he has burned the near minions, the beam is free.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Yasuo for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: Drop the black hole between you and Yasuo — the pull drags him off his dash line and the centre executes him if he stays under the threshold.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks and you are airborne for Last Breath.

edits.before: Your flight is your only escape — a W spent poking is a death sentence against the next gank.
edits.after: Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1; Sweeping Blade is back in 0.5s — you cannot outrun him without it.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: Every minion beside you is a 475 dash he can chain, and Steel Tempest costs him nothing on a 4s cooldown to spam through them.

notes: The two layers were asserting opposite facts about the single most-cited interaction in this matchup. The full layer's tldr says Wind Wall does NOT block the beam; content said in four places that it negates your poke entirely. The kit settles it: Wind Wall blocks projectiles, and no Aurelion Sol ability carries the projectile flag, so it blanks your support and covers his approach but does nothing to your own damage. I corrected content to the full layer, not the reverse. Also fixed a reversed mechanic: spikes[1] claimed Last Breath 'resets his own knockup chain' when Riot's text says it resets all stacks of Gathering Storm — it clears them. Chart rows 5 and 6 moved Yasuo -> Aurelion Sol in the full layer to match content and the packet, with phases[5].why rewritten in the same proposal; phases[6].why already argued for Aurelion Sol under a row labelled Yasuo, so that row was self-contradicting before this edit. Yasuo is male per champ-gender.
